source.title: Intriguing Properties of Adversarial Examples
source.authors: E. Cubuk; Barret Zoph; S. Schoenholz; Quoc V. Le

page_placements.theme: Memorized-label fitting and perturbation robustness are distinct

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study trains a fully connected network on randomly shuffled MNIST labels to perfect training accuracy, bearing on random-label fitting, and measures adversarial error in that setting. It does not reproduce the original studies' broader evaluation.
record.gate_note: The study also reports adversarial error results for many other models and datasets, but those do not bear on the claim versions. Figure 2(b) reports the shuffled-label model's adversarial error on the training set; it does not measure test error at chance.
record.test_reason: Section 2 reports its own shuffled-label MNIST training experiment reaching perfect training accuracy, using the original claim's random-label fitting method and training-accuracy measure. The subsequent adversarial evaluation addresses a different question.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for the shuffled-label experiment: its training-set adversarial error follows a power law, which the authors interpret as evidence that the scaling does not require meaningful dataset content or generalization. The broader paper also concludes that architecture affects adversarial robustness, which correlates strongly with clean accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: This paper studies adversarial error and logit differences; the shuffled-label experiment measures FGSM adversarial error on the training set rather than reproducing the original studies' full random-label generalization evaluation.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack protocol changes the observed power-law exponent.

fits_no_version.finding: FGSM adversarial error on the shuffled-label model's training set follows a small-perturbation power law with exponent 1.2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Power-law adversarial vulnerability persists in a network that perfectly memorizes randomly shuffled labels.

record.problems: The shuffled-label fitting result is stated without an exact accuracy percentage. The text does not report test error or compare the model's settings with a true-label training run.
record.rows_left_out: No other results bear on the claim versions. The paper reports many adversarial-error measurements for other models and settings, but those concern adversarial robustness rather than random-label fitting.

untested.parts: Chance-level test performance, use of stochastic gradient optimization, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters relative to true-label training.
Relative training time and convergence as label corruption increases.
Perfect fitting of shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs; the random-logit analysis does not test input fitting.
Training and test error across increasing fractions of corrupted labels.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Whether shared real-data patterns are learned before noisy labels.

record.verdict_notes: Training on shuffled targets is the manipulation required to test V1. The study reports achieved fitting accuracy, so its downstream use of the fitted network does not make it solely T4. No missing results bear on the other versions.

versions.untested_parts: The text does not report test error at chance or establish whether architecture and training hyperparameters were unchanged from a true-label setting.
